references.text: The mountain burned with fire all the way to heaven, with darkness, clouds, and thick fog - the same darkness (עֲרָפֶל) that surrounded God's presence on Sinai
Moses stood between the Lord and the people because the people were afraid of the fire and did not go up the mountain - parallel to the people standing at a distance
The Lord said he would dwell in the thick darkness (עֲרָפֶל) - the same word is used for the cloud where God was present
The Lord said he would dwell in the darkness (עֲרָפֶל) - parallel to God's presence in the thick cloud
The Lord made darkness his hiding place, with dark clouds around him - a poetic description of God's presence in the darkness
Clouds and darkness are around him - describes God's majestic presence enveloped in darkness
Reference to the Sinai event with fire, darkness, storm, and trumpet sound, and the people's fear of hearing more
Illuminates the same theological principle of God's holy distance; 19:17 sets the scene for the conclusion of 20:21.
Retells the same event from different angles; both illustrate God's hidden presence that requires a mediator.
24:2 is the direct instruction that explains the action in 20:21; both emphasize the principle that only the mediator can approach God's holy presence.
